evidence: Consolidate tested local interpretations without promoting them to recovered hardware semantics.

annotations.name: call-fed loop entry
annotations.meaning: 01C pushes 01D; BLT at 01E consumes that entry.
annotations.limitations: Control-flow interpretation; not a counted-loop algorithm identification.

annotations.name: terminal tail
annotations.meaning: Helper calls and computed dispatch lead to the unconditional self-branch at 084.
annotations.limitations: No physical completion or restart protocol identified.

annotations.name: register right-shift helper
annotations.meaning: Four RAM right-shift destinations followed by return; Q is not shifted.
annotations.limitations: Register identities depend on A/B roles; not proven serial output.

annotations.name: conditional Q drain
annotations.meaning: Right-shift Q and store shifted value; loop exit can test zero.
annotations.limitations: Local current-flag fixtures take at most eight shifts. The fitted previous-flag policy can take nine; not a proven multiplier.

annotations.name: preparation with disputed register roles
annotations.meaning: Candidate D,Q operations write R0 repeatedly or R10-R13 with swapped roles.
annotations.limitations: External D selection and destination registers remain hypotheses; caller effects depend on the mapping.

annotations.name: paired add/subtract and permute
annotations.meaning: Four-entry tables combine paired 16-bit operands using sums/differences and permutation.
annotations.limitations: Output grouping is virtual; no physical write enable or DAC destination identified. Identities were search constraints.

annotations.name: paired quarter-turn transform
annotations.meaning: Four entries produce (X,Y),(-Y,X),(-X,-Y),(Y,-X) modulo 65536.
annotations.limitations: Tested with local nonzero operands; reset-call source pairs in earlier studies were zero. Identities were search constraints.

annotations.name: source-overlapping transform
annotations.meaning: Writes overlap source Y; independent quarter-turn interpretation fails.
annotations.limitations: Do not extend the independent transform formula to this table; source aliasing changes later reads.

annotations.name: nested computed-call wrapper
annotations.meaning: Wrapper reaches computed call 2C4 and returns at 2C5.
annotations.limitations: Reachability requires site-scoped ROM-table hypotheses; unrestricted nesting overflows.

annotations.name: conditional adjustment selector
annotations.meaning: Selects the 2D9 or 2DC adjustment tail.
annotations.limitations: Disconnected from reset in the current graph; condition select 2 meaning unknown.

annotations.name: transient one-unit adjustment
annotations.meaning: The two tails differ by one in first Y and converge to equal modeled state at 07B.
annotations.limitations: Local probes only. No first-Y consumer identified; wrapper paths differ by one cycle.

annotations.name: ROM-backed dispatch candidate
annotations.meaning: Scenario supplies targets from lookup-ROM bytes plus explicit banks.
annotations.limitations: Site, bank, range and index source remain hypotheses; see current table provenance in the listing.

annotations.name: successor-byte wait preparation
annotations.meaning: In the tested reset path, 18D loads external X into R3 and 19C stores its complement in R4 for the later poll.
annotations.limitations: Requires the tested previous-flag reset path, zero Q at 18D and zero carry at both writes; physical input source unknown.

annotations.name: external-byte equality poll
annotations.meaning: Under previous-zero loop control, wait until D+R4 is zero modulo 256, then return. The tested caller makes this a successor-byte wait.
annotations.limitations: Flag timing is hypothetical; physical input channel and protocol unknown. Current-flag control tests a different value.

annotations.name: paired Q drains
annotations.meaning: Load and drain shifted S+C and S from R4; preserves R1-R15 and clears Q/R0 in tested local fixtures.
annotations.limitations: Previous-zero condition, zero shift fill and original register roles; transient ALU outputs may matter externally. Not an established multiply/divide or physical delay.

annotations.name: input-dependent biased Q shift
annotations.meaning: Shift Q and emit biased R0 values; termination depends on external D and R7 under the previous-flag policy.
annotations.limitations: Local caller-249 fixtures only. R7=FF gives exact repeated states for most constant-D/Q combinations; actual caller preconditions and external channel unknown.

annotations.name: three-loop shift wrapper
annotations.meaning: Calls two right-shift loops and one left-shift loop without initializing R7; constant-D fixtures often repeat.
annotations.limitations: Original-role previous-flag and zero-fill assumptions. Seeded reset dispatch reaches the wrapper with R7=FF and Q=D; physical dispatch and external-input behavior remain unresolved.

annotations.name: input-matched left shift
annotations.meaning: Left-shift Q until previous F=D+Q is zero; after return clear Q and write D+1 to R0.
annotations.limitations: Original-role previous-flag and zero-fill assumptions. Seeded reset dispatch reaches the wrapper with R7=FF and Q=D; physical dispatch and external-input behavior remain unresolved.

annotations.name: input-code dispatch candidate
annotations.meaning: At first tested reset entry current Y=(D+1) mod 256; optional current-Y indexing selects one of eight following branch words.
annotations.limitations: Current-Y indexing is an alternative scenario; default index remains scenario-supplied. Physical D and address source unknown; no claim for every later visit.

annotations.name: carry-controlled three-add loop
annotations.meaning: Chain three byte additions into R1/R2/R3 while outputting old A values; previous-flag BLT repeats on middle carry.
annotations.limitations: External operands and output consumers unknown. Current flag timing selects last carry instead; defaults unchanged. Constant reset inputs in the tested dispatch path repeat.

annotations.name: idempotent Q-mask tests
annotations.meaning: Mask Q with R0 and test containment under previous flags; 126 adds R10 before and after its loop. Failed tests repeat without selecting external D.
annotations.limitations: Defined logical carry and previous-flag policy. Current timing tests a different predicate; reset-derived non-return cases constrain the hypothesis rather than prove hardware hangs.

annotations.name: masked external-byte equality poll
annotations.meaning: Under q2 and previous-zero loop control, mask Q with R0 then wait until external D equals the masked value.
annotations.limitations: Shared previous-flag and defined logical-carry policy. Modeled reset reaches a zero target with explicit external replies; physical D and nonzero target provenance unknown.

annotations.name: carry-qualified external wait
annotations.meaning: Under q2 and previous-carry control, repeat while R0+D carries; tested reset R0=FF makes this a wait for D=0.
annotations.limitations: Shared previous-flag policy and diagnostic external replies; physical source and protocol unresolved.

annotations.name: captured-register copy and paired-arithmetic loop
annotations.meaning: Under q2, copy R4–R7 into R8–R11, call the paired-arithmetic table, and repeat while its final high-byte result is nonzero. Independent reset-captured low/high bytes in R6/R7 reach R10/R11; addition may return with a nonzero low-byte result.
annotations.limitations: Previous flags, top-level index 5, preceding-Y dispatch at 38F and diagnostic per-site reads. First pair is zero and second operands are equal in these reset runs. Physical output and dispatch wiring remain unresolved.

annotations.name: preceding-Y paired-arithmetic dispatch candidate
annotations.meaning: q2 computes D−R14 immediately before a paired-arithmetic call. Optional preceding-Y indexing selects its add/subtract combinations; current Y and Q are zero in tested reset paths.
annotations.limitations: Site-scoped preceding-Y hypothesis with fixed top-level dispatch 5 and early input replies; physical index wiring and output consumer remain unresolved.

annotations.name: accumulator carry and threshold gate
annotations.meaning: Under q2, snapshot old Q in R0/R5, preserve R3 in R2, complement R1 into R3, and add D to Q. Addition carry gates transform calls; old Q versus R7 selects the call sequence.
annotations.limitations: Shared previous-flag policy. Nonzero-Q carry paths are local fixtures; tested reset executions skip every transform call. Repeated Q-to-R0 writes at 341–344 remain a candidate-specific decode.

annotations.name: fixed-source transform high-byte loop
annotations.meaning: Under q2, copy R0 to R1 and repeatedly transform R10–R13 into R4–R7. Previous-zero control returns when the second result high byte is zero; sources and Q remain unchanged.
annotations.limitations: Constant dispatch index and shared previous-flag policy. Failed conditions repeat rather than converge; nonzero source/caller cases are local fixtures, with physical loop condition and output meaning unresolved.

annotations.name: source-overwriting transform loops
annotations.meaning: Under q2, 3D5 overwrites X with the second transform result; 3EA overwrites Y with its first result. Real previous-zero loop control yields one/two-pass returns or exact 8/16-instruction cycles.
annotations.limitations: Constant dispatch and shared previous-flag policy; nonzero states are local fixtures. 3EA sequential aliasing changes its formulas; physical output meaning and reset reachability remain unresolved.

annotations.name: cleared-Q single-iteration shift helper
annotations.meaning: q1–q4 clear Q after loading D+Q, store shifted (R0+1) in R5, and return with R0/Q zero after one loop iteration.
annotations.limitations: Original register roles, previous-zero control and zero shift fill. Input effects disappear from final internal state; physical transient consumers and reset caller operands remain unresolved.

annotations.name: masked-Q two-bit drain helper
annotations.meaning: fitted_original masks Q with R0, stores shifted (R0+masked Q+1) in R5, and drains Q two bits per iteration. Previous-zero timing requires a final zero-entry iteration.
annotations.limitations: Previous-zero policy and zero shift fill; one to five iterations in local fixtures. Physical operation and reset caller operands remain unresolved; swapped register roles are not covered.

annotations.name: double drain and input preparation prefix
annotations.meaning: Two drain calls clear R0/Q and overwrite first R5 before any selected consumer. Two 311 calls retain the second external byte in R12; final preparation copies R10/R11 under q2 or external bytes under fitted_original.
annotations.limitations: Local 304 entry: the shared select-5 stub at 302 bypasses this path from 300. Stops at 309 before the next wrapper; external consumers of transient values remain unidentified.

annotations.name: register-difference scan and carry wait
annotations.meaning: Expose selected register differences against R0 without changing RAM/Q. With shared constant-zero select 6, the first two loops run once; previous-carry control repeats the last loop iff R15>=R0.
annotations.limitations: Shared select-5/select-6 stubs and previous-flag policy. Reset index 3 exercises the scan, including fitted_original D=FF repetition; physical output consumers and condition wiring remain unknown.

annotations.name: conditional entry into adjustment tail
annotations.meaning: With the optional composed BRT gate, a set previous-zero flag at 2D8 selects fallthrough into 2D9–2DB. Reset index 2 reaches this tail under both tested mappings.
annotations.limitations: Requires the optional address-bit gate and combined dispatch tables; not enabled by default. Physical gate wiring and transient output consumers remain unknown.

annotations.name: conditional register-copy tail entry
annotations.meaning: Under fitted_original and the optional composed gate, previous zero at 0F9 can enter 0FA, which copies R0 to R2 before the 0FC branch to 078. One reset fixture reaches this path.
annotations.limitations: Witness uses dispatch index 3 and D=FF; R0/R2 are both zero at the copy. Default entry remains unresolved, and no physical gate or nonzero copy use is established.

annotations.name: conditional difference tail
annotations.meaning: Preserve RAM/Q while exposing Q-R0, optionally Q-R0-1 when Q complements R0. Under the optional gate, branch to 287 for nonzero preceding difference, otherwise fall through to 3C0.
annotations.limitations: Exhaustive local R0/Q pairs assume previous zero at entry to 3BC. Reset entry demonstrated only under q2 with D=01 and indices 12 modulo 16. Optional gate and output consumer remain unverified.

annotations.name: Q-zero conditional tail
annotations.meaning: Under q2 reset states with R0=FF, expose Q-1/Q and branch at gated 2CE according to the previous Q zero flag. Q=0 falls through into 2CF, exposing D+Q+carry without storing it.
annotations.limitations: Reset entry uses optional BRT gate, constant dispatch index 12 and diagnostic zero read at 2A8. Q-driven dispatch instead routes Q=0 elsewhere in the tested scenario. Physical input, output consumer and gate wiring remain unidentified.

annotations.name: conditional Q decrement tail
annotations.meaning: Under q3, expose Q and optionally Q-1 when Q complements R0; gated 3BF branches to 287 for a nonzero preceding result. RAM/Q are preserved.
annotations.limitations: Local rule assumes previous zero at 3BC. Reset index 12, D=01 reaches 287 with R0=FF/Q=00 under the optional gate; hardware decode and output consumer remain unknown.

annotations.name: transient Q and register differences
annotations.meaning: Under q3, expose Q-1, Q, R2-R0 and R12-R0-1 in sequence without changing RAM/Q, then continue to 28B.
annotations.limitations: Reset entry depends on q3, the optional BRT gate and index-12 D=01 diagnostic scenario. Physical output consumer is unidentified; default entry labels remain unresolved.

annotations.name: zero-sum entry and carry-selected adjustment
annotations.meaning: Under q2, load R0=D+Q and R3=~R1; expose R0 at 254. An extended optional gate admits 256 when R0=0. Previous logical carry from XNOR(0,Q) selects 2DC for Q=FF and 2D9 otherwise.
annotations.limitations: Matched reset sweep uses Q-indexed 26F and diagnostic reads at 2A8/235/251. The three-bit gate is a branch-address correlation, not recovered wiring. Output consumer and default entry remain unresolved.

annotations.name: transient difference before preparation re-entry
annotations.meaning: Under q2, expose Q-R0 without storing it, then re-enter the preparation call at 259. The four-bit gate extension supplies a reset witness with Q=FF, R0=0 and an empty live stack.
annotations.limitations: Requires the optional four-bit clause and diagnostic input scenario. The external output consumer remains unknown; default reachability stays unresolved.

annotations.name: register copy and Q-zero continuation
annotations.meaning: Under fitted_swapped, copy R2 to R0, then test Q through the previous zero flag. Nonzero Q branches to 078; Q=0 exposes ~R15&R0 and R0 before the 0FF branch to 07B. Q and other RAM are preserved.
annotations.limitations: Requires diagnostic relaxation of the entire 0FC identical-word class and fixed-false select 6. Clean index-3 reset witnesses do not eliminate the conservative underflow paths at other aliases. Output consumer and physical wiring remain unknown.

annotations.name: masked-input continuation test
annotations.meaning: Under q3/q4, expose R4-R0/R4 respectively, then load Q from the AND of two external reads. Preserve RAM and continue at 2E6 iff Q equals R0-1 modulo 256, otherwise branch to 2FD.
annotations.limitations: Requires the diagnostic alias gate, previous flags and fixed-false select 1. Clean zero-reset entry is shown at FF; other input bytes in the same sweep underflow at 2FF. No physical input protocol or globally safe gate is established.

annotations.name: shifted-Q preparation and nested dispatch
annotations.meaning: Preserve Q; prepare R0=Q>>1, R2=D_2C2+Q and R4=((D_2C0+Q) mod 256)>>1. Expose R5+Q immediately before the nested call; expose current Q-1 at the outer return.
annotations.limitations: Nonzero states use local actual-call fixtures; five zero-reset witnesses enter with Q=R5=0. Scoped ROM table, zero-fill shifts and previous flags remain hypotheses. Physical index and output consumer unknown.

annotations.name: nested input-load and Q-exposure leaves
annotations.meaning: Entry 224 exposes R15 before 225 loads Q from D and exposes R0 AND R3 and Q. Entries 229/22B/22C/22D preserve Q and RAM while exposing Q and/or Q-1 before returning.
annotations.limitations: Validated as nested leaves of the q2 2BC wrapper with explicit nonzero local fixtures. Arithmetic outputs have no identified physical consumer; no integrated reset coverage claim.

annotations.name: nested input-sum capture and carry-qualified return
annotations.meaning: Store D+Q in R15 twice, expose differences, then test carry from Q-R0. The 2BC caller prepares R0=Q>>1, forcing the branch to 227 and preserving Q.
annotations.limitations: The forced branch is specific to the prepared calling state; 2B9-2BB are not globally dead. Nested input is constant per fixture. Other profiles and physical output are unresolved.

annotations.name: save R0, optional Q load and byte sum
annotations.meaning: Save old R0 in R3; select-6 skip optionally suppresses loading Q into R0. Return with R15=(R0+2*R1+1) mod 256, preserving Q and all other RAM. Five q2 reset traces connect the R0 copy to the following XNOR/skip decisions.
annotations.limitations: Both select-6 outcomes are explicit local condition stubs; reset witnesses use fixed-false select 6. No physical consumer is identified for the transient or retained R15 result. Other mappings decode these instructions differently.

annotations.name: two indexed register stores
annotations.meaning: Copy R1 into R2, prepare Q>>1 twice, and store it into two selected RAM registers. Under preceding-Y indexing, a first store into R6 changes the base for the second address. The second helper overwrites a first R5 store; a second R5 store restores the value.
annotations.limitations: A constructed input contract exhausts all Q bytes/destination pairs from a verified reset checkpoint. The index source and PC-keyed inputs remain hypotheses, not a recovered board protocol or physical output.

annotations.name: half-Q and input-difference preparation
annotations.meaning: Preserve Q; write R0=Q>>1 and R5=((D-Q-1) mod 256)>>1 under zero-fill shifts. Expose D-R6 on Y at the return, providing a candidate index for the next computed call.
annotations.limitations: Constant D per local fixture; zero-fill and carry policy remain hypotheses. Repeated shifts do not shift Q, and no serial-output role is established.

annotations.name: indexed R0 copy and return
annotations.meaning: Sixteen one-word POP entries copy R0 into R0 through R15 respectively. The q2 terminal caller supplies Q>>1 as the stored byte.
annotations.limitations: The inferred table is exercised by scenario/current-Y/Q/preceding-Y candidates. Register writes do not establish a physical DAC transfer or index wiring.

annotations.name: reset input accumulation in Q
annotations.meaning: Each word adds its external D byte into Q with carry zero. From zero reset, the two reads produce Q=(D_002+D_076) mod 256 before the first 109 dispatch.
annotations.limitations: Input reads are explicit stubs. Independent-input reset prefixes are verified under q1/q3 only; other mappings do not share this input dependence. Physical input timing and source remain unknown.

annotations.name: Q-based input-sum dispatch candidate
annotations.meaning: Q-indexed first dispatch selects entry (D_002+D_076) mod 8. Current Y equals Q under q1 and Q+1 under q3 in the tested reset prefix; preceding Y also reflects the input schedule.
annotations.limitations: Index source remains an explicit candidate. Equal input bytes create a parity restriction that independent reads remove. Handler entry is verified, not complete handler behavior or a physical command protocol.

annotations.name: eight-way handler branch table
annotations.meaning: The eight branch words select handlers 11A, 148, 18B, 300, 259, 345, 09E and 133. Independent q1/q3 input sums reach each through the actual 109 dispatch.
annotations.limitations: Uses the default unconditional-transfer policy, not optional BRT gates. No physical opcode assignment or full handler algorithm is established.

annotations.name: handler-2 external-byte comparison
annotations.meaning: Previous flags wait for D=-R4 modulo 256. With input-sum handler-2 reset entry, q1 R4=s-2 and q3 R4=FE; a matching reply returns and reaches 084.
annotations.limitations: Diagnostic input schedule, fixed other dispatch indices and previous-zero condition. Physical byte channel and protocol remain unknown.

annotations.name: preserved-R0/Q transform-loop predicate
annotations.meaning: Current-zero loop control repeats iff R0 & Q is nonzero. Wrapper and all four candidate table entries preserve R0 and Q. Handler-2 reset entry gives R0=Q=s != 0, so later D replies or table choices cannot release it.
annotations.limitations: Scoped to the four decoded table entries and current-zero policy. Previous flags test a different value; not an unconditional claim about hardware execution.

annotations.name: input-sum preparation with overwrite
annotations.meaning: 314/316 write D+Q to R13; 315/317 write D+Q to R4. In handler-5 zero-reset runs, the final 317 input supplies an independent first arithmetic component; earlier R4 loads are overwritten.
annotations.limitations: Previous-flag diagnostic reset schedule with Q=5. Physical meaning of D and any transient external consumers remain unknown.

annotations.name: paired-component copy and final-high-byte loop
annotations.meaning: Copy R4-R7 to R8-R11 and call paired arithmetic. Previous-zero exit observes only the last high byte. q3 reset inputs supply independent U byte and V word; both output results, including the first high byte, may be nonzero on return. q1 matched inputs retain a zero first component.
annotations.limitations: Operands within each pair are equal after the wrapper copies; first component high byte is zero on entry. Diagnostic inputs, previous-Y dispatch and virtual output captures do not recover physical ports.

annotations.name: ROM-address/carry feedback loop
annotations.meaning: With the two-bit ROM-read gate, R0=FF and previous carry timing, the next lookup address is R2 exposed on Y at 36E. A finite recurrence explains constant-reply exits and cycles: 215 bytes return and 41 cycle from the demonstrated reset state.
annotations.limitations: Scoped to bank-256 previous-Y ROM reads at gate-selected words and default D=1 outside 36D. Not a recovered handshake protocol or signal-processing algorithm.

annotations.name: computed-call return wrapper
annotations.meaning: 2FD exposes an ALU result, 2FE calls 21A, and 2FF returns to the pre-existing caller. Under the retained dispatch tables, exactly one incoming frame supports all nested alternatives within the four-entry stack.
annotations.limitations: Calling-convention interpretation. No incoming frame causes underflow after a normal callee return; two or more can overflow on nested choices. Local graph safety does not prove all-input termination.

annotations.name: difference-based tail-call guard
annotations.meaning: 3BB writes R5=old_R5-R0-1 modulo 256. With conditional previous-zero 3BC, unequal old_R5 and R0+1 selects the return wrapper at 2FD; equality falls through.
annotations.limitations: Requires 3BC to be conditional under the scenario gate. A branch into 2FD is not safe with an empty caller stack after a normal 21A return. Physical condition gating remains unresolved.

annotations.name: Q-exposing nested-dispatch preparation
annotations.meaning: Increment R4, copy R1 into R2, expose Q at 21E, call a ROM-backed table at 21F, and return. Input masks 51/A3/F5 from actual reset reads select 2BC through Q; previous Y has the same value while current Y is zero.
annotations.limitations: q3 input schedule and retained 82-entry lookup hypothesis. Earlier dispatches remain seeded scenario choices; this does not recover the physical index source.

annotations.name: nonzero masked-input nested preparation
annotations.meaning: In the verified nonzero-mask reset context, preserve Q=m, prepare R0=m>>1 and R4=((CC+m)&FF)>>1, and overwrite temporary R2 with R5=0. Q or preceding Y selects the inner ROM call, reaching 22B or 225 with real depth-four stack use.
annotations.limitations: Three nested mask cases from a 256-mask reset sweep. q3 differs from q2 at 2C2; formulas are scoped to the documented input and register context. Physical protocol and table wiring remain hypotheses.

annotations.name: direct-byte indexed half-Q stores
annotations.meaning: Prepare Q>>1 and store it twice through the 08A register-copy table. Under preceding-Y dispatch, 089 exposes the external destination byte unchanged. First R6 does not alter the second address; first R5 is overwritten by the second helper.
annotations.limitations: Verified after the A3 masked nested reset prefix with diagnostic PC-keyed input bytes. Physical destination wiring and output consumer remain unknown.
